children.text: Once the largest U.S. Air Force base outside the United States, this city has been transformed into a freeport zone of wide lawns and tree-lined avenues, where you can enjoy it all at once: an airport with direct flights from Korea, resorts and golf courses, and the food of Pampanga, the culinary capital of the Philippines.
Clark is a freeport zone straddling the cities of Angeles and Mabalacat in Pampanga. It began in
as Fort Stotsenburg, a U.S. Army cavalry post; Clark Field was built in
, and the site hosted a U.S. military base (Clark Air Base) until
. During the Cold War it was one of the largest U.S. military bases outside the U.S. mainland, but in
the eruption of Mount Pinatubo buried the base in volcanic ash, and that same year the Philippine Senate rejected the extension of the bases agreement, so the U.S. military withdrew. In

it was designated the Clark Special Economic Zone, an economic free zone managed by the Clark Development Corporation (CDC), and an airport, industrial parks, resorts, casinos, and golf courses followed. Part of the former base is still used by the Philippine Air Force under the name Clark Air Base.

Traces of the base era remain in many places today. The sprawling lawns of the old parade ground, the straight roads lined with acacia trees, and the low-rise houses and restaurants converted from former officers' quarters create a relaxed atmosphere completely unlike hectic Manila. With little traffic congestion and well-managed security, it's also a city with a large population of retirees, long-term expat families, and Korean residents.
Since Clark International Airport (CRK) opened a new passenger terminal in
, it has been linked by direct flights with Korean cities such as Incheon and Busan, becoming a gateway for starting a trip to northern Luzon without passing through Manila. It takes only
10–20 minutes
by car from the airport to a hotel in the city, so it is easy to start traveling on the day you arrive.

Pampanga, home to Clark, is a region Filipinos themselves call the "culinary capital." Signature Filipino dishes like sisig, tocino, and burong kanin were all born here. You can combine the convenience of an airport city, the history of the base era, Pampanga's food, and side trips to Pinatubo and Subic, making it a great fit for family trips, golf trips, and short weekend getaways alike.

As a destination, Clark is easiest to understand as three areas: the main Clark area, home to the Parade Ground, museums, resorts, and water parks; Angeles's old downtown (Santo Rosario), with its church, old mansions, and sisig restaurants; and the Fields Avenue nightlife strip in Balibago, just outside Clark's main gate. East of the airport, the business district of Clark Global City is growing, and to the north, in Capas, Tarlac, lies New Clark City, home to the main stadium of the
Southeast Asian Games. A typical plan is one day for Clark itself and Angeles's food scene, and another for a nearby trip such as Pinatubo or Subic.

Angeles is the birthplace of sisig, chopped pig's head grilled on a hot plate. Visit the old restaurants considered the originators of sisig and traditional eateries in San Fernando to taste authentic Kapampangan cuisine.
This vast lawn was the parade ground in the base era, and today it is busy with locals enjoying sunset strolls, jogging, and picnics. A
2.2 km

rubberized jogging track runs along its edge, and the old gateposts of Fort Stotsenburg, the cavalry equestrian statue, and the red star-shaped Clark sign are popular photo spots. It's best explored together with the old base buildings around it.
The museum sums up Clark's history at a glance, from the Spanish era through the U.S. military base and the Pinatubo eruption to its transformation into a freeport zone.
1–1.5 hours

is enough. Building 2097 next to the Parade Ground also houses a 4D theater and a visitor information center, making it a good place to pick up Clark maps and event information. Opening days and admission fees differ from source to source, so check before you visit.

children.text: The Philippines' biggest aviation festival, launched in
and held near Clark around
February
each year. The 26th edition in
was held on
February
13–15 in New Clark City, Capas, Tarlac; the venue and dates change each year, so check the announcements.

The Aqua Planet water park covers about 10 hectares with at least 38 rides and attractions, and is open only Thursday through Monday (closed Tuesdays and Wednesdays). A one-day pass for guests 122 cm and taller costs about
on weekdays and about
on weekends. Dinosaurs Island, a park full of dinosaur models, is open daily from
8 AM–6 PM
with bundled tickets at about
, while Sandbox in Porac has a giant swing and a roller-coaster-style zipline.

Clark and its surroundings have several 18-hole golf courses that draw many Korean golf travelers. The 36-hole Mimosa Plus, Clark Sun Valley, and Fontana are inside Clark, and Luisita in Tarlac City is about
1 hour
away by car. Weekday green fees are cheaper than in Korea and travel distances are short, though caddie and cart fees are paid separately.
Holy Rosary Church, whose construction began in
, became Pampanga's first minor basilica in
. Near the church stands the Pamintuan Mansion, built in
, where General Aguinaldo celebrated the first anniversary of independence on
; today it is the free-admission Museum of Philippine Social History (closed Mondays). You can explore it all on foot, as far as the Museo ng Angeles, housed in the old city hall built in

This hot spring lies in a volcanic ash canyon of Mount Pinatubo west of Clark: you ride a 4x4 jeep across the lahar (volcanic mudflow) fields, then enjoy hot spring baths, a volcanic sand bath, and a mud pack. Packages including lunch start from about
per person for groups of four or more, and opening hours are
9 AM–5 PM
(last entry
2 PM
). It can't be reached on foot, so a reservation is required.

children.text: Arrive at Clark International Airport, drop your bags at a hotel near the airport, and take a Grab to Angeles's old downtown
Visit Holy Rosary Church and the Pamintuan Mansion (Museum of Philippine Social History)
Late lunch at an original sisig restaurant such as Aling Lucing
Sunset walk on the Parade Ground, photos at the Stotsenburg equestrian statue and the Clark sign
Dinner at a restaurant in Clark, rest at your hotel, and board a domestic flight to El Nido, Coron, or Siargao the next morning
Clark International Airport (CRK) has direct flights with several Korean cities including Incheon and Busan, with a flight time of about
4 hours

. Domestic flights also connect to Cebu, Davao City, Boracay (Caticlan), Palawan, and more. Routes and airlines change by season, so check the latest schedule. From the airport to a hotel in Clark, it's
10–20 minutes
by taxi or hotel pickup.
Since
March 29, 2026
, propeller aircraft have been banned from Manila airport, so Cebgo's small-aircraft routes have moved to Clark. As a result, you can take direct flights from Clark to
El Nido
Coron
(Busuanga),
Siargao
, Naga, and San Jose (Mindoro), and in particular the direct flights to El Nido from Luzon now depart from Clark rather than Manila. PAL Express, a Philippine Airlines affiliate, also flies the
Batanes
(Basco) route. Korea routes include direct flights from Cheongju in addition to Incheon and Busan. You can check routes on the
official Clark International Airport website

From Korea, Jeju Air, Jin Air, and Asiana Airlines fly direct to Clark from Incheon, and Jin Air also flies direct from Busan. Other international routes include Tokyo (Narita), Hong Kong, Singapore, Taipei, Bangkok, Dubai, and Doha, while domestic flights connect Clark with Cebu, Davao City, Iloilo City, Bohol (Tagbilaran), Puerto Princesa, and Caticlan. Clark airport handled a record of about 2.75 million passengers in

The easiest way from Manila is the airport-link P2P bus. Buses (Genesis and others) run from NAIA Terminal 3, PITX, Trinoma, Cubao, and other points to Clark International Airport and SM Clark, taking about
2.5–3 hours
, with fares of about

depending on where you board. To travel cheaply, take a northbound bus such as Victory Liner from Cubao or Pasay, get off at the Dau terminal in Mabalacat, and then take a jeepney or taxi into Clark (bus about
P2P bus fares differ by departure point. From NAIA Terminal 3 and PITX it is about
(the Joybus, with wider seats and a toilet, costs more), and from Cubao and Trinoma about
. The PITX route was newly introduced on
March 17, 2026

, and most buses pass through SM Clark and stop at the arrivals level of the airport passenger terminal. If you have an early-morning or late-night flight, check the timetable in advance. P2P bus fares rose by about 15% on
September 28, 2026
, and the amounts above are rough figures that reflect the increase.
From Baguio, Genesis (Joybus) runs several buses a day to Clark International Airport, taking about
3–4 hours
, with fares of about
depending on the class. From Subic and Olongapo, Victory Liner runs to Clark, taking about
2–3 hours
, for about

September 28, 2026

From Manila, it's about
north on NLEX, taking
1.5–2.5 hours
. NLEX tolls rose on
January 20, 2026
: the Balintawak–Dau section costs

for a Class 1 car, and more if you connect via Skyway or SCTEX. Toll plazas mainly use RFID (Easytrip) electronic payment, so if you're driving a rental car, check its sticker and balance. Inside Clark, the roads are wide and quiet, making driving easy.

Within Clark, getting around is mainly by ride-hailing services such as Grab and by taxi. The Clark Loop shuttle bus runs between SM City Clark and Clark International Airport with 25 stops, and instead of paying cash you tap a beep card when you get on and off. The airport advises passengers to pay only the metered fare for airport taxis. In Angeles town, jeepneys and tricycles are the main transport, costing about
for short trips.
Clark's dry season is
November–April
December–February
has cool mornings and evenings and clear skies, best for outdoor activities, and
February
brings the hot air balloon festival with plenty to see.
March–May
is the hottest stretch of the year, with midday temperatures climbing to around 35°C, so it's best to mix indoor sightseeing with outdoor activities.
June–October
is the wet season, with strong afternoon showers, and
July–September

can see several days of rain in a row due to typhoon effects. If your trip is mostly city sightseeing and food, the wet season isn't too inconvenient, but Pinatubo tours are often suspended during this period.
Year-end in Pampanga is special. At the Giant Lantern Festival in San Fernando, held around
mid-December

, you can see the spectacle of enormous Christmas lanterns (parol) made of thousands of light bulbs twinkling in time with music. During Holy Week, some Pampanga towns hold religious events reenacting actual crucifixions, drawing large crowds.

and may vary depending on local conditions.
Accommodation falls into two main areas. The Clark Freeport Zone is home to casino resorts, golf resorts, and international chain hotels, and it is quiet and safe, with rooms at about

per night. Representative international chain and casino hotels include Clark Marriott, Swissôtel Clark, Hilton Clark Sun Valley Resort, and Midori Clark. Angeles town and the area around Fields Avenue have plenty of cheap hotels at

per night, but they are close to the nightlife district, so for family trips we recommend staying inside Clark or near the malls. Long-term visitors sometimes rent serviced apartments or condos by the month.
Food is at the heart of any trip to Clark. Aling Lucing, where Lucia Cunanan first served today's sizzling sisig of grilled, chopped pig's ears and cheeks beside a railroad crossing in Angeles in

, is still going strong on Glaciano Valdez Street, and Mila's Tokwa't Baboy on San Andres Street is also counted among the best sisig spots. Everybody's Cafe in San Fernando is a long-established restaurant that has served traditional Kapampangan dishes since

, where you can try frog dishes, kare-kare, and dishes served with burong kanin. Tocino (sweet cured pork), longganisa sausage, and the traditional Pampanga sweets turron and sanikulas are also popular souvenirs.
As a city with a large Korean community, Clark also has many Korean restaurants, Korean grocery stores, and Korean-style cafes, which come in handy when you're craving Korean food on a long trip.
When you arrive at Clark International Airport, use the official taxi counter or a hotel pickup. Checking the fare in advance helps you avoid getting overcharged.
Clark is spread out and difficult to get around on foot. Install a ride-hailing app or consider a daily vehicle charter (about
For currency exchange, money changers inside malls generally offer better rates than the airport. ATMs are plentiful at large malls like SM Clark.
Sisig varies in style from restaurant to restaurant. Try comparing the traditional version without mayonnaise to the modern version topped with an egg.
The hot air balloon festival in
February
peaks around
6 AM
, when the balloons all rise together. Traffic control is heavy, so use a shuttle or set off early.
The lantern festival in San Fernando in
December
takes place at night and gets very crowded on weekends. Aim for a weekday evening instead.
It's convenient to split your schedule by time of day — malls and museums during the midday heat, and a walk on the Parade Ground in the late afternoon.
If you're planning a Pinatubo tour, arrive in Clark the evening before and get an early night. Pickup around
3–4 AM
is typical.
The Pinatubo Kapas route requires foreigners to have a Philippine Air Force visit permit, so you must send your passport photo page to the tour operator
at least 35 days
before your visit. Book before you come to Clark.

Inside Clark, the CDC Public Safety Department enforces against speeding, not wearing a seatbelt, and running traffic signals 24 hours a day. If you've rented a car or motorcycle, be sure to obey the posted speed limits.
In the wet season (
June–October
), when the southwest monsoon coincides with typhoons, the low-lying areas of southern Pampanga flood extensively. In
July 2025

, about 520,000 residents of 290 barangays in Pampanga were affected by flooding, so when the rain keeps up, check PAGASA forecasts and road conditions before heading south to places such as San Fernando.
The area around Fields Avenue in Angeles is a nightlife district. Family travelers should avoid this area late at night, and always keep an eye on your belongings and drinks.
Prostitution is illegal in the Philippines and carries very heavy penalties. Don't respond to solicitation.
Some taxis try to negotiate a fare instead of running the meter. Prefer a ride-hailing app or hotel car.
At casinos, offers of gambling-related loans or offers to accompany you are very likely scams.
Outdoor activity at midday during
March–May
carries a high risk of heatstroke. Drink water often and rest in the shade.
During the hot air balloon festival in
February
, the lantern festival in
December
, and the street festival in
October
, crowds pour in, pickpocketing increases, and roads around the venues are closed. Carry your valuables in front of you and arrange your ride back in advance.
About
1–1.5 hours
by car. A popular day tour by 4x4 and trekking up to the emerald crater lake.
About
1 hour
by car (via SCTEX). A former U.S. naval base where you can enjoy jungle experiences, a marine theme park, and beaches.
About
1 hour
by car. A solitary extinct volcano rising from the Pampanga plain, with legends and trekking trails.
About
2 hours
by car. A heritage resort in Bataan built from relocated old Philippine mansions.

30–40 minutes
by car (via NLEX). The capital of Pampanga, famous for the Giant Lantern Festival in
